definition: Deliberately attacking an AI system to find failures, vulnerabilities and harmful behaviors before real users do.
details: Red teams try jailbreaks, prompt injection, data leakage, tool abuse and harmful-generation attempts, then feed the findings back into safety training and guardrails. It adapts security's adversarial-testing practice to language models, and models are increasingly used to red-team other models.
story: Picture a parachute packed by a second pair of hands: nobody plans to need it, but everyone is glad it was checked. The idea is simple: before something powerful is let loose, someone checks that it will not do real harm to real people. It is the habit of asking, before every launch, what could go wrong — and then doing something about it. Caution is not the enemy of progress — it is the reason progress gets to keep going. And that is AI Red Teaming — the reason we can move fast without breaking things, or people.

citation.title: Red Teaming Language Models with Language Models
